en.title: St. Anton next week: a powder top-up of 5–45 cm (snow forecast 23–29 November 2026)
en.description: St. Anton snow forecast for 23–29 November 2026: 25 cm at the top (5–45 cm), 18 cm at the base, snowiest day Sunday 29 November, with neighbours compared.
en.lede: The question for anyone heading to St. Anton next week is simple: how much, and where? Between Monday 23 and Sunday 29 November our forecast puts 25 cm on the upper slopes (5–45 cm), 25 cm around 2000 m and 18 cm at the base, with Sunday 29 November as the snowiest day.

p: The first instalment comes this week: 24 cm on the upper slopes of St. Anton from 17 to 20 November, 12 cm lower down. Next week adds a second layer on top.

sections.h: What falls where on the St. Anton slopes
p: Read from the top down: 25 cm near 2500 m, 25 cm near 2000 m, 18 cm near 1400 m. The low-to-high spread is 5–45 cm at the top and 4–31 cm at the base.

Day by day, the upper mountain picks up most of it on Monday 23 (5 cm, up to 6), Wednesday 25 (3 cm, up to 4), Thursday 26 (6 cm, up to 13) and Sunday 29 (9 cm, up to 17). Outside those days expect little more than flurries.

sections.h: Snow or rain at the bottom?
p: Little is lost on the way down: 18 cm around 1400 m against 25 cm up high. On these numbers the precipitation falls as snow almost everywhere in St. Anton.
St. Anton is the steep end of the Arlberg, where off-piste traffic tracks out fresh snow quickly.
For comparison, the upper slopes of the closest big resorts collect Lech-Zürs (11 km away) 30 cm, Ischgl (19 km away) 18 cm and Davos (43 km away) 16 cm; St. Anton sits at 25 cm.
The differences are small: the storm covers this whole corner of the Alps evenly, so pick on terrain and lifts, not on the snow total.

sections.h: When and where to ski St. Anton
p: If you can pick one day, take the one that follows Sunday 29 November, when 9 cm (up to 17 cm) has landed on the upper mountain.

Go high: depth is safest on the Valluga and the Kapall ridge, and the best skiing should be on the shaded Rendl side and the north-facing slopes under the Valluga. Treat the Nasserein end of the village as the weak point.

sections.h: The range, not just the number
p: Treat this one with caution: 5 cm at the low end, 45 cm at the high end. A spread that wide a week out means the storm may still slide away from St. Anton or sit right over it.
Storm timing tends to firm up first; totals keep moving until a day or two before.

advice: Fresh snow on a young snowpack: read the regional avalanche service of the province before any off-piste plan.
Check the resort's own opening date and lift status: snow on the mountain does not mean lifts are running.
Watch the forecast midweek: the top's range is 5–45 cm.
